subject: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance

messages.author: 9af6d8f650589d7d
messages.subject: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
parts:
Hi Ed, 

Consider the model below:

model <- '
    x ~ lzx*z
    y ~ lxy*x
    w ~ lzw*z

    x ~~ cxz*z
    y ~~ cyz*z
    w ~~ cwz*z
    y ~~ cwy*w'


Is there an easy way I can put a uniform prior, say [-.2, .2] on the error covariance cwz? 

Relatedly, does the package provide a function for plowing prior vs posterior distribution of a parameter?

Thanks. 

Best, Carlos

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Setting uniform prior on specific error covariance
parts:
Carlos,

Regarding the prior on the covariance: blavaan breaks up the
covariance into something like

sd_1 * sd_2 * corr_12

and then you put a prior on these three terms (the two
variances/standard deviations/precisions, along with the correlation).
So it is easy to put a prior on the correlation, but not the
covariance. But there is a trick here: the correlation is between -1
and 1, but there are few distributions with support on (-1,1). So you
have to use a distribution with support between 0 and 1 (typically
beta distribution), which is then automatically translated to a
distribution with support on (-1,1).

But this is a little funny for a uniform prior. In that case, you have
to figure out that uniform(.4,.6) on (0,1) becomes uniform(-.2,.2) on
(-1,1). So the syntax would look like

w ~~ cwz*z + prior("dunif(.4,.6)")*z

And then you might still have trouble with initial values, because any
(random) starting value outside of (-.2,.2) might crash the model. In
this case, maybe try the option inits="simple". But I would recommend
instead using a beta prior where most of the density lies between .4
and .6 under (0,1) support.

Re plotting: there is currently no automatic way to plot prior vs
posterior. I notice the bayesplot package makes some of the plotting
stuff easier but have not explored it much yet.

Ed

I think the easiest way to visualize it is something like

hist(-1 + 2*rbeta(1e4, 3, 3))

where you can change the rbeta parameters as desired.

Ed
